newsitem.title: INDIA: India new gold import rule effective from Jan 1.
newsitem.headline: India new gold import rule effective from Jan 1.

text.p: The Indian government said the easing of a gold import restriction, announced earlier this week, took effect on Wednesday and the customs duty remained unchanged.

On Tuesday, the Press Trust of India (PTI) said the government had allowed non-resident Indians to import 10 kg of gold every six months compared to five kg previously. The news agency did not say when the change would take effect.
"The enhancement limit of 10 kg up to which gold can be imported by passengers would come into force from 1st January, 1997," the statement said.
It said the rate of customs duty would remain unchanged at 220 rupees ($6.13) per 10 grams (0.35 ounces).
PTI quoted Finance Minister P. Chidambaram as saying the easing of the import restriction would curb smuggling, shore up gold reserves and bring in more revenue from import duties.
India lifted a ban on gold imports in 1992 and gradually liberalised gold trade.
